scope: early_load_core with DCACHE=1 and ICACHE=1 (L1 cache plan Tasks 5-8). Cacheable loads, early only (with EARLY_LOADS=1 every cacheable non-faulting load is early), read rtl/memory/l1_dcache.sv: 1 KiB, 2 ways x 16 sets x 32-byte lines, write-back, write-allocate, one miss outstanding, at most two loads tracked by the LSU and answered by id in any order. MMIO/uncached loads, stores and address faults keep the head path; the cache's line traffic shares the data port through the LSU's port mux. Store path (Task 6): a retired cacheable store enters a 4-entry store buffer (rtl/memory/store_buffer.sv) at retirement; the buffer writes its head into the cache's write port in retirement order, and each entry stays a forwarding candidate (age 0..3, older than every queued store) through its landing cycle. Retirement of a cacheable store waits while the buffer is full; MMIO and faulting head accesses wait for it to be empty. committed_valid_o pulses with the buffer head as it lands. FENCE.I: head_system_controller waits for order (empty buffer), pulses the cache clean and waits for its end. A refill or writeback access fault is fatal (ruling A1). Instruction side (Task 8): fetch reads rtl/frontend/l1_icache.sv (1 KiB, 2 ways x 16 sets x 32-byte lines, read-only, one line transaction) on the existing instruction port, once per line into its line buffer; an idle line checks the next line with a cache prefetch and a hit fills the ahead buffer. FENCE.I invalidates the instruction cache one cycle after its clean ends, before its redirect; from the time it reaches the head until then, no new instruction-port request starts.
verification: Sail and Spike lockstep differentials of fetched_core_tb on this profile (plus the directed recovery_during_load_miss, mmio_bypasses_dcache and store-buffer programs with perf witnesses), ACT4 on the fetched core, the directed fence_i_after_store program, cpi-check and coremark-check, store-buffer-check, load_store_unit_dcache_tb, l1_dcache and l1_icache unit checks, the fetch_unit ICACHE bench, the fetched-core store-check tests (including refill faults), RTL assertions.
